title: Falsification of Crash Test Results by Japanese Carmaker and Impact on Cars in Singapore
what_it_is: Falsification of Crash Test Results by Japanese Carmaker and Impact on Cars in Singapore

sections.label: Daihatsu crash test falsification checks
sections.summary: LTA checked vehicle records and dealers and found no affected Daihatsu vehicles registered or sold in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is aware of the admitted falsification of crash test results by a Japanese vehicle manufacturer – Daihatsu – and has taken action to identify whether any of the affected cars are sold and driven in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, LTA cross-checked against its vehicle records and found that none of the affected vehicles, based on the published chassis numbers by the vehicle manufacturer, have been registered in Singapore to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Second, the relevant motor dealers have confirmed that they did not sell any of the affected vehicles.

sections.label: Affected Daihatsu models and engines
sections.summary: The committee identified 64 affected models and three engines, but LTA found no affected vehicles registered or sold in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The committee, as the Member has noted, identified 64 vehicle models, which included the Daihatsu models as well as models produced by Daihatsu but supplied as OEM models to Toyota, Mazda and Subaru, and sold as the respective makes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Three engines, including those that had already been discontinued were affected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But, as mentioned in my reply, the LTA checked and there was no vehicle registered in Singapore that fall within the affected chassis range reported in the recall of these vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Beyond just checking our vehicle register, we reached out to Toyota Motor Asia Pacific as well as their authorised motor dealers for the various mix to confirm that they have not sold any of these affected vehicles to date.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, as it is, there is no cause for concern in this respect.

sections.label: LTA monitoring and follow-up actions
sections.summary: LTA will monitor the issue and work with Toyota Motor Asia Pacific and dealers on follow-up if affected vehicles are found.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: LTA will closely monitor the developments of this issue and subsequently, if we do find any affected vehicles and if they are identified, we will work with the Toyota Motor Asia Pacific as well as the relevant authorised motor dealers for the necessary follow-up actions.
